extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and reviewers (investigators, program staff, potential reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the NIH peer review process, scoring, review criteria for research project grants, and requirements for rigor and reproducibility for applicants and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and error correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Once submitted to NIH, your application is checked for completeness. Errors related to application processing are flagged by Grants.gov and errors related to the application requirements are detected by the eRA system. Any errors identified at this stage must be addressed and the application resubmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is important to submit early so that errors can be corrected prior to the submission deadline!

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with FOA instructions and NIH formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are manually checked by NIH staff for fit with the NIH mission, overlap with other applications you may have under review, and compliance with the FOA instructions and NIH formatting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with all NIH guidelines could result in the withdrawal/rejection of your application by NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate study section assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Receipt and Referral handles the receipt of grant applications and the assignment of applications to a Scientific Review Group (SRG) or study section. It is important to identify a study section that is appropriate for the review of your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can indicate their preferred study section and funding institute as part of their application using the PHS Assignment Request Form (ARF). Use tools like the Assisted Referral Tool to match your title/abstract/aims to appropriate study sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-level peer review process (first and second level roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH utilizes a two-level peer review process: the first level is managed by CSR or an IC and is carried out by a study section; the second level is carried out by each NIH IC Advisory Council/Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Advisory Council considers IC research priorities, program staff input, overall impact scores, percentile scores (if applicable), and summary statements before making funding recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring: 9-point rating scale and scoring procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH grant application scoring system uses a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) in whole numbers (no decimals) for Overall Impact and Criterion (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) scores for all applications, with a score of 5 considered an average score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers submit preliminary scores prior to the study section meeting often used to determine which proposals are discussed; after discussion, final impact and criterion scores are submitted. The final overall impact score is calculated by multiplying the mean of the final impact scores by 10 and reported on the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile score
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile is the approximate percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from a given study section over the past year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentile scores, when applicable, are considered by Advisory Councils along with impact scores and summary statements in recommending funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for endorsement before funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Only applications that are endorsed by the study section, program staff, and the Advisory Council are recommended for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final funding decisions are made by the Directors of the respective NIH Institutes and Centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an Overall Impact score that reflects their evaluation of the potential for the project to impact the relevant research field, as determined by their assessments of the scored review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall Impact is informed by Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, and Environment criterion scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance is one of the scored review criteria for research project grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate scientific premise as part of the Significance criterion and assess whether the applicant has discussed the strengths and weaknesses of the foundational data and described how the proposed research will address identified weaknesses or gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) is one of the scored review criteria for research project grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether the investigators are well qualified to carry out the proposed work (guidance and templates available on OER site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation is one of the scored review criteria for research project grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether the project uses novel concepts, approaches, or methodologies (additional guidance available on NIH OER).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach is one of the scored review criteria for research project grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess scientific rigor as part of the Approach criterion, evaluating experimental design, controls, plans to reduce bias (blinding, randomization, inclusion/exclusion criteria), power analyses, and statistical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment is one of the scored review criteria for research project grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether the institutional setting and resources will contribute to the success of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Premise (Rigor & Reproducibility component)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific premise for an application is the research that is used to form the basis for the proposed research question(s). NIH expects applicants to describe the general strengths and weaknesses of the prior research being cited by the applicant as crucial to support the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This consideration should include attention to the rigor of previous experimental designs, incorporation of relevant biological variables, and authentication of key resources. Reviewers evaluate scientific premise as part of the Significance criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Rigor (Rigor & Reproducibility component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific rigor is the strict application of the scientific method to ensure robust and unbiased experimental design, methodology, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of results. This includes full transparency in reporting experimental details so that others may reproduce and extend the findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess scientific rigor as part of the Approach criterion and the overall impact score, including evaluation of experimental controls, bias reduction plans, power analyses, and statistical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of relevant biological variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Biological variables, such as sex, age, weight, and underlying health conditions, are often critical factors affecting health or disease. Reviewers assess the applicant's plans to address relevant biological variables, such as sex, as part of the Approach criterion score and the overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant proposes the use of only one sex, reviewers will assess the justification provided by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Key biological and/or chemical resources include cell lines, special chemicals, antibodies, transgenic animals, and other biologics. These resources may differ across labs or time and may influence research data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers discuss the adequacy of the plan for key resource authentication after scoring; comments on authentication should not affect scores. Nonetheless, if the authentication plan is inadequate or missing, it will be reflected in the written critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Policies and Practices considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Review Policies and Practices include information on peer review regulations and policies, including conflict of interest, rigor & reproducibility, human subjects and vertebrate animals, and scoring procedures for research applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and applicants should consult these policies for compliance issues that affect review and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility and Early Career Reviewer (ECR) selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered for the ECR program, individuals must have 2 years of experience in a full-time faculty or research position, show evidence of an active independent program of research, have at least two recent senior-authored research publications, and may have not served on a CSR study section (mail reviews are not counted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current funding is not required. Participation as a reviewer also allows NIH reviewers to submit certain grant applications on a continuous basis as an incentive.
